channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Nearly 40% of drivers in Belgium avoid cities because of parking problems
item.description: Three in four respondents find street parking (too) expensive, and 83% think it is just a “cash cow” for authorities.

item.title: Workers' Party shakes off links to Friday's Brussels riots
item.description: Raoul Hedebouw condemned the accusations calling Friday's aggressive rioters the Workers' Party's "shock troops."

item.title: Wallonia-Brussels Federation finally agrees to expand juvenile facilities
item.description: Ministers promise 56 new places by 2028 after prosecutors said youth suspects had to be freed for lack of space, raising fresh questions over the credibility of the justice system.

item.title: 2026 Climate March kicks off in Brussels
item.description: Tens of thousands have joined the afternoon walk to take a stand against Belgium's perceived lack of ambition on climate action.

item.title: 60 apartments evacuated in Brussels blaze
item.description: A fire sparked by rubbish at the base of an external staircase led to an overnight evacuation in a block of 60 flats. The cause of the blaze has not yet been determined.

item.title: Manneken Pis dressed in special 'climate change' costume
item.description: Organisers expect about 30,000 people at today’s climate march, after activists used a high-profile city landmark to press for a political shift and insist that climate is also a matter of security.

item.title: Minors released from Brussels juvenile detention due to overcrowding
item.description: Eight minors, including a teenager with seven ready-to-use Molotov cocktails, have been released from a Brussels youth detention facility.

item.title: African women protest against genital mutilation in Brussels
item.description: Many women in Belgium remain at risk, mostly from countries such as Ghana or Guinea.

item.title: Electric police car burns down in Brussels
item.description: Three people were temporarily evacuated after an overnight fire damaged two police vehicles and part of a station building. The cause remains unclear, with experts called in to determine whether a fault was involved.

item.title: Bushcrafting weekend in Brussels sells out in four minutes
item.description: The event teaches children and adults how to live in nature while emphasising the need for more well-managed, resilient natural space.

item.title: 30% of intercity trains cancelled on Monday amid strikes
item.description: Student trains on Sunday evening will run as normal, but Monday commuters face widespread disruption as the rail operator warns of sharply reduced services.

item.title: Over a dozen arrested after violent protests in Brussels
item.description: 21 people, including 17 minors, were placed under judicial arrest after violence before a trade union march had properly begun. Prosecutors cited arson, vandalism, weapons offences and armed resistance.

item.title: Tensions flare in Brussels Government over funding for social housing
item.description: Tensions flared inside the Brussels government on Thursday over extra funding for the Brussels Regional Housing Corporation (BGHM).

item.title: Police deploy tear gas and water cannon against riots around union protest Brussels
item.description: Belgium’s two biggest trade unions, CSC-ACV and FGTB-ABVV, are staging protests on Friday against the federal government’s budget plans.

item.title: Trade Unions refuse Bouchez's request to postpone protests
item.description: The trade unions' protests on Friday and Monday are aimed at probable budget cuts and reforms by the federal government.

item.title: More than 13 kilograms of cannabis found during search in Jette
item.description: Police in Jette seized 13.53kg of cannabis, seven bottles of GHB and €8,670 in cash during a search of a flat on Tuesday, arresting two suspects.

item.title: More than a quarter of schools in Brussels overexposed to NO₂
item.description: "It is unacceptable that, in Brussels, going to school still means being exposed to toxic fumes."

item.title: The Brussels Times Gig Guide: What are the best concerts this October?
item.description: Check out this month's unmissable gigs in the Belgian capital for your and your friends to enjoy.

item.title: Fake cannabis shops in Brussels linked to Telegram drug dealers
item.description: An undercover conversation by The Brussels Times and one of these 'businesses' uncovered the scale of these operations.

item.title: Ixelles commune introduces free parking permits for garages blocked by roadworks
item.description: The new permits will apply when roadworks affect a parking space for at least 10 working days.
